The Mr. Rabbit Magic Show is a joyful, colorful celebration made for Rusty Lake's 10th anniversary, and it wears that spirit proudly. Rather than another moody escape-room mystery, this one leans into pure puzzle-solving — a series of short, inventive "acts" built around Mr. Rabbit's tricks, each one clever and satisfying in its own bite-sized way.

What really makes it special is how lovingly it nods to the series' history. I had a blast spotting references and easter eggs tucked into nearly every corner. And just when you think you've got the game figured out, it finds a fun way to surprise you — I won't say more than that, but it's a nice reminder that Rusty Lake still knows how to keep players on their toes, even in a lighter, more playful package like this one.

It's free, it's short, and it doesn't take itself too seriously — but it's clearly made with a lot of care for longtime fans. A fun, charming love letter to the series.

I feel awful sh!tting on this birthday celebration, but I don't really feel like this game is up to par with Rusty Lake's other work. I wish Rusty Lake a happy (late) 10th Birthday, and I absolutely love the other Rusty Lake games, but I did not really enjoy this one. If you're not a devout Rusty Lake fan, I would skip this one and play one of their other games.

Here's what I didn't like:
- There were too many trial-and-error based puzzles. At least four of them, which is just tedious and annoying.
- The game felt very silly for a Rusty Lake game. I understand it's a birthday celebration but it just doesn't fit.
- There were multiple things in the game that were misleading and/or served no purpose.
- It was long and drawn out for a free, celebratory game. Everything went too slow. and honestly there was too much. It was a full-length experience without the full weight of any other Rusty Lake game.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐This game made me question my intelligence… in the best way possible.

I went in expecting a cute little puzzle game… and came out wondering how the developers managed to hide clues in places I had looked at 10 times already. 😭

There were so many moments where I was like, “Okay… I’m actually dumb.” Then I’d accidentally click something and suddenly…

“WAIT… THE CLUE WAS HERE THE WHOLE TIME?!” 🤯

That’s what makes Mr. Rabbit Magic Show so brilliant. The puzzles are fair, clever, and reward observation instead of random guessing. Every tiny detail exists for a reason, and when everything finally clicks together, you feel like an absolute genius… until the next puzzle humbles you again. 😂

The art style is ridiculously adorable. Every room is packed with charm, every animation is smooth, and the magical atmosphere never stops putting a smile on your face. You can genuinely feel how much love and care went into every single scene.

The best part? The game never holds your hand, but it also never feels unfair. Every solution makes you go:

“OH MY GOD… IT WAS SO OBVIOUS!”

followed immediately by:

”…How did I miss that?” 💀

That’s the magic of this game.

10/10. Cute, clever, relaxing, hilarious (mostly because of my own brain), and one of the most satisfying puzzle experiences I’ve played in a long time.

And seriously… don’t stop with this one. Go check out the other main games from Rusty Lake too. After experiencing this masterpiece, I honestly can’t wait to dive into the rest of their games. If this is the level of creativity they consistently deliver, I’m already a fan. 🐰🎩❤️

A wonderful celebration of the Rusty Lake series and the folks behind it.

I must say this game took me on a surprise rollercoaster, transforming from another Rusty Lake title to a package of easter eggs and details nodding to previous titles, as well as other game the Dev team has worked on outside of this series.

I was taken by surprise when the game transformed beyond the magic show into your character helping to continue 'developing' the game, within a game. My favorite details were in the office where you could take a look at various artifacts from the Rusty Lake series, both mainly on the shelves and scattered around the room. My personal favorite is the in-game photos on the phone of the Dev team, it's a personal favorite of mine when you get to see the team behind something within a title. I also love the attention to detail when the player interacts with the phone being able to break the 4th wall.

Overall, the length of the puzzles and their difficulty were just right. Although I did find the knife puzzle a bit trivial, the rest of the puzzles were very intuitive and followed a similar pattern known if you have played any previous titles. The Dev team and their Rusty Lake series will always hold a special place in my gaming history as one of the first titles that captivated mean back on flash alongside the Henry Stickman series and a Small Favor series.

I think it is one of the best puzzle games I have ever played, and I would highly recommend it. The game drops you into a mysterious magic performance filled with hidden secrets, where you sit in the audience and watch Mr. Rabbit perform on a small stage. While the show unfolds, you will constantly interact with the stage as you play, clicking on the magic hat, opening curtains, and exploring different props. Every small action can trigger something unexpected, which makes it feel like the performance is alive and reacting to you. What I really like is how the game keeps making me question what is real and what is just part of the trick. Each act feels like a short puzzle, but there are almost no direct instructions, so you are always observing carefully and trying things out on your own. The atmosphere is also very unique. It starts off cozy and playful, almost like a charming little magic show, but slowly it begins to build layers of mystery and a subtle sense of unease.
